title: Lionel Hampton first asks him to join in 1939
summary: Hampton asked Cobb to join after hearing him play Body and Soul, but Cobb asked for $500 advance and heard nothing; by 1942 Hampton wanted him again.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I was there for 5 months. We worked in the Rum Boogie. Ken [Bloods] who was the manager of the

Regal Theatre in Chicago was a very good friend of Lionel Hampton's. Lionel had called him -- well, see, Lionel had asked me in Houston to join his band, and I just got married during that time in the year of 1939, and he wanted to hear me play without a microphone, "Body and Soul" -- he said he heard about my big horn, as he said.

Him and Marshall Royal were together up there -- that's the Eldorado Ballroom. And I played it. And then he asked me to join the band, and well, I had heard from different musicians that he'd only get you out on the road and they would strand you there, and I was with like a family band where we all got along together, but if you ask any leaders for any money in advance, then you didn't get your job.
So I told him, I said, "Man, I have need $500 worth of debt -- if you can advance me $500, I'll pay my debt off and I'll be glad to come and join you." And I ain't heard no more from him.
And what they told me was right.
Was he married to Janice then?
You better know it. I can give you a story on that, too, but I'll talk about that later.
So that went on. That was in '39. So this is in '42, I'm getting to. That is 3 years later, and he still wants me. See, Illinois had cussed him out and he wanted to get rid of him.
